exit_code_rule: A restore of a staged tracked member from HEAD that still fails after 3 tries makes cleanup_staged print ONE ERROR line naming every tracked file left carrying staged content and return 1; the in-loop call then does `exit 1` before any further member is staged, and the EXIT trap (cleanup) remembers the failure in RESTORE_FAILED_FILES and, whatever else happened (including a script that otherwise succeeded and was exiting 0), ends the script with the status it already had if that was non-zero, otherwise 1; a restore that succeeds, and a build that stages nothing tracked, take none of these branches and keep their exit codes and output lines unchanged.
failure_message_sample: ERROR: could not restore from HEAD (3 tries); tracked file(s) left carrying staged content: fn1/src/mod1.py
retry_choice: RETRY ADDED: up to 3 tries of the git checkout HEAD restore with a 1 second sleep between tries (2 seconds in total), because the observed cause is a transient .git/index.lock held by another seat's commit; a failed third try ends exactly as the no-retry rule says (ERROR line naming the files, non-zero exit). Arm (a) holds the lock for the whole run, so it exercises the full three tries.
arms: a-restore-blocked-exits-nonzero-and-names-file: tracked member, pin != HEAD, .git/index.lock held: rc non-zero, exactly one ERROR line naming fn1/src/mod1.py, the tracked file still carries the pinned bytes
b-restore-ok-exits-zero-tracked-equals-head: same member, no lock: rc 0, no ERROR, file equals HEAD, git status clean
c-stages-nothing-tracked-exits-zero: no staged_from (lock held anyway): rc 0, BUILD_ONLY line, Complete (BUILD_ONLY), no ERROR
d-no-further-member-staged-after-failed-restore: two functions, lock held: rc non-zero, the second function's member is never staged
e-no-aws-call-made: the stub aws log is empty after every arm
negative_control: The same test run against the base build-and-upload.sh (git show 2d923d0564:infra/aws/lambda/ci/build-and-upload.sh copied beside the test in a scratch dir): arm a FAIL (rc=0, no ERROR line), arm d FAIL (rc=0), arms b, c, e PASS, test rc 1.
